_about: The ONLY geometry primitives we can build. The CAD tool offers a fixed block library and we can place nothing else, so every chamber and channel in chip/*.json must map to a block id below. 'Multilayer' blocks are deliberately absent: we print a SINGLE fluidic layer, so no block that needs a second layer, a via or a crossing is usable. tools/check_chip_spec.py enforces this list, the single-layer rule and the build envelope.

envelope.note: Resin 3D printing plus hot embossing, one fluidic layer, 30 x 20 mm build area.
envelope._two_scales: TWO envelopes. chip/ is built to the DEMO one (30 x 20 mm), which is what we can print today. target_envelope (200 x 300 mm) is the agreed maximum for the real device. Scale-free rules carry over unchanged; the rest are listed under target_envelope.

fabrication_floors.note: From the fabrication review. Print open and seal with film rather than printing an enclosed channel below 0.5 mm.

basic.serpentine_channel: Folded run: length (resistance or residence time) in a small area.
basic.port: Through-hole to tubing. The only fluid inlet/outlet.
basic.curved_y_junction: Y with swept arms, lower shear than a sharp Y.
basic.trap_chamber: Chamber with retention features at its outlet.
basic.flow_focusing_funnel: Tapered funnel into a narrow throat.
basic.flow_divider: Splits a stream into set fractions.

advanced.pillar_array: Regular pillars: filtration, support, or holding a lid flat.
advanced.pillar_funnel_trap: Funnel into a pillar gap; traps a particle at the throat.
advanced.dld_array: Deterministic lateral displacement: sorts by size continuously.
advanced.lock_and_shift_trap: Captures then releases on flow reversal.
advanced.metering_trap: Captures a FIXED VOLUME. The block for metered splitting.
advanced.round_sorting_junction: Size/inertia sorting at a round junction.
advanced.centipede_channel: Many short side branches off a spine.
advanced.herringbone_mixer: Chevron grooves; chaotic advection mixing at low Re.
advanced.spiral_channel: Archimedean spiral; inertial focusing or long path.
advanced.phase_guide: Capillary pinning ridge; stops a liquid front at a defined line.
advanced.wagon_wheel_port: Port with radial spokes; even feed, resists collapse.
advanced.gradient_generator: Tree network producing a concentration gradient.
advanced.angiogenesis: Parallel channels separated by posts, for sprouting assays.
advanced.tesla_valve: Passive flow diode. USELESS BELOW Re 1: diodicity is exactly 1.0 in Stokes flow, so do not use it for rectification at our flow rates.

excluded.multilayer: All 15 multilayer blocks. We print one fluidic layer, so anything needing a second layer, a via, a membrane or a crossing channel is unavailable. This is why no chip may route two channels across each other.

retention._problem: The smallest feature we can print is 200 um IN PLANE. A capsule is 70 um, swelling to 140 um. So no printed in-plane gap can retain a capsule, and every 5-30 um mesh in the old designs is unbuildable. On-chip washing depends on retention, so this decides whether washing works at all.
retention.solution: DEPTH WEIR. The 200 um floor applies to WIDTH, not to z: a crest 240 um tall leaves a 60 um gap under the lid, which retains a 70 um capsule while liquid passes. It is still ONE fluidic layer, because the crest is relief in the same mould or print, exactly like the print-open-and-seal-with-film rule above. Prior art: Harrison/Oleschuk weir bead traps (US 7,312,611).

weir_geometry.rule: gap must be STRICTLY below trap.gap_factor_high (0.4) x capsule diameter (70 um) = 28 um and at or above trap.gap_factor_low (0.3) x D = 21 um. 25 um sits inside that band. tools/check_chip_spec.py enforces the upper bound with >=, so a gap equal to it fails.
weir_geometry.untested: No published capture efficiency for weirs retaining particles above 100 um. Run a coupon with 40, 60 and 80 um gaps before committing. z tolerance of +/-20 um is a 33% error on a 60 um gap.
weir_geometry.z_tolerance_warning: A 28 um gap in a 300 um layer is the hard part. Published z tolerance on these processes is around +/-20 um, which is +/-71% of the gap, so the weir could close or leak outright. THIS IS THE BIGGEST UNKNOWN IN THE RETENTION SCHEME. Run a coupon before committing. If it fails, the lever is capsule size: capsules are tunable 35-260 um, and a larger capsule allows a proportionally larger, more printable gap.
weir_geometry.crest_height_rule: crest = that CHIP's etch depth minus the gap. It is NOT a fixed number: a 272 um crest cannot exist in a 150 um layer, and chips have different depths. Derive it per chip.

alternatives_ranked: dld_array as a CONTINUOUS WASH rather than retention: at gap 200 um and eps 0.125 the critical diameter is ~105 um, so swollen capsules displace and unswollen ones do not. Needs +/-10 um gap tolerance.

Bought woven nylon mesh insert (5 um and up) clamped in a recessed ledge. The 200 um floor does not apply to a bought part. Use only where retention below 50 um is needed. Adds a manual assembly step.
Sedimentation sump: keep upward velocity below the ~50-210 um/s settling speed, which caps exchange at roughly 6-9 uL/min in a 0.3 mm x 15 mm channel. Works, but slow.
Off-chip centrifuge. Works today but breaks the nothing-off-chip claim.
retention.not_viable: pillar_array and pillar_funnel_trap cannot retain by size exclusion at a 200 um throat. Stagnation-point traps need active feedback and were published for 1-15 um beads.
retention._cells_caveat: This weir retains CAPSULES (70 um). It does NOT retain a bare cell of 10-15 um. Any chip that washes cells rather than capsules needs a different answer: see protocols/retention_audit.md.

target_envelope._decision: Design target is the ANSI/SLAS 1-2004 microplate footprint, 127.76 x 85.48 mm. Three lanes at 1,200 mm2 need 3,600 mm2, which is 33% of it, so the area we actually require fits with room for the PCR dock and the extraction region. 200 x 300 mm stays recorded as the absolute ceiling, but nothing in the design needs it.
_why_not_600: Yield did not need it: 1e5 cells is about 1,200 mm2, a 35 x 35 mm lane.

Concentration does not improve with area. An adherent chamber holds about 277 cells/uL whatever its size, because that is density divided by height, so a flow-through extract is roughly 36x too dilute at ANY board size. The fix is trap-and-elute, not area.
Risk concentrates in a monolith: at 90% per-lane weir yield, 3 lanes work 73% of the time and 36 lanes 2.3%. Parallel chips lose a lane, not a board.
600 mm does not fit a CO2 incubator shelf (about 450-500 mm), which weeks-long culture needs.
Embossing 600 x 600 mm needs roughly 70 tonnes and a non-desktop press.
target_envelope.what_it_buys: 60,000 mm2, 100x the demo. Three lanes at 1,200 mm2 each is 3,600 mm2, about 6% of the board, so culture area stops being the limit and there is room for the PCR dock, the extraction region and spare lanes.
design_rules_at_this_scale: KEEP CHAMBER LENGTH CONSTANT and replicate chambers. Residence time is NOT scale-free: at fixed shear the velocity is fixed, so a longer lane has proportionally longer residence time.
Extraction happens AFTER concentration, never in the culture chamber. Size the extract by cells/1e4 microlitres, not by chamber area.
Support the lid with a pillar_array at about 5-10 mm pitch, or a 0.3 mm chamber spanning hundreds of mm collapses under bonding and operating pressure.
The 6-port limit is a demo constraint and lifts here: ports can sit on an area grid, so lanes get dedicated feeds, drains and sampling lines instead of sharing off-chip selectors.
The 98 C index PCR stays a small zoned dock. Heating the whole board would expand it by millimetres and cook the culture.
scale_free: wall shear at fixed flow per unit width
not_scale_free: flow distribution across a wide weir
_why_sbs: No mainstream cell-culture microfluidic device is larger. Mimetas OrganoPlate puts 40 three-lane chips on ONE SBS plate; Emulate runs 12 chips per array. The field repeats small units inside a standard outline rather than making one big chip.

It unlocks off-the-shelf hardware: plate handlers and stackers, readers, imagers, liquid handlers on the 9 mm ANSI/SLAS 4-2004 pitch, incubator shelves and robot grippers. That matters for the stated goal of running with no human intervention.
It fits every desktop resin printer, so prototyping stays cheap. A 200 x 300 mm part fits NONE of them - the largest desktop build is about 353 x 196 mm - and would force CNC plus a large press.
It is inside the hot-embossing comfort zone (rigid platens are fine to about 200 mm; 300 mm is the hard edge).
target_envelope._caveat: ANSI/SLAS fixes the outline and well positions, NOT well-bottom height, so SBS size alone does not guarantee a plate reader or imager will focus on the chip. Check working distance.
target_envelope._ceiling: 350 x 190 mm is the agreed MAXIMUM chip size, chosen to fit the largest desktop resin build area (Formlabs Form 4L, 353 x 196 mm) with a few mm of margin, so prototyping stays on a desktop machine. It is 66,500 mm2, 111x the demo. CONSEQUENCE: at 350 mm the part is past the rigid-platen hot-embossing edge (comfortable to about 200 mm, hard edge about 300 mm), so embossing at full size needs a large-platen press (Collin P500S class, 496 mm, 785 kN - the part needs only 66-200 kN) or gas-pressure tooling. Note Obducat's large-area gas tool caps at 160 C, below the ~170 C used for some COC grades. Nothing in the current design needs this size: three lanes require 3,600 mm2, which is 33% of an SBS plate.
